description: This line plot, titled “Ablation Study on HateXplain Dataset,” illustrates the performance of five model variants on three evaluation metrics—Precision, Recall, and F1-score—expressed as percentages. The x-axis, labeled “Model Variants,” is categorical and lists five conditions in order: “Full model (Ours),” “w/o Prompt,” “w/o Augmentation,” “w/o Attention,” and “w/o Prompt & Augmentation.” The y-axis, labeled “Metric (%),” is linear, ranging from 56% to 66%, with major gridlines and tick labels at 58, 60, 62, 64, and 66. Three distinct lines represent the metrics: Precision (purple line with circular markers), Recall (light blue line with circular markers), and F1-score (brown line with circular markers). For the “Full model (Ours),” Precision is 65.78%, Recall is 65.96%, and F1-score is 65.49%. Removing the prompt causes Precision to drop to 61.06%, Recall to 59.64%, and F1-score to 60.16%. Without augmentation, Precision rises slightly to 62.75%, Recall peaks at 63.63%, and F1-score is 62.22%. Removing attention results in Precision of 64.06%, Recall of 59.17%, and F1-score of 59.67%. Finally, removing both prompt and augmentation yields Precision of 65.44%, Recall of 56.82%, and F1-score of 57.74%. The plot visually demonstrates how each component affects the model’s performance across the three metrics.
